Sofia — appreciate the clear ask and the schedule. Two quick things from our side:

1) Standard three-year prepay tiers give larger cumulative discounts but we don't normally front-load more than 40–45% in year 1 without an exec approval because of revenue recognition and capacity planning.
2) A 45% discount in year 1 materially impacts the overall unit economics; I'll need to loop in finance and commercial leadership.

I've attached our latest term sheet and a draft SOW for their review. Can you confirm Novus is comfortable with a partial non-refundable prepay for year 1? That helps justify the concession.

I'll escalate this for a decision today — copying Marissa and Vivek for fast-track review. If you can confirm final signature party and billing entity that helps too.

Thanks,

Rishi / Vivek —

I reviewed the numbers. If Novus wants 55% prepaid in Y1 with a 45% discount for that tranche, we need executive sign-off for:

- One-time customer credit (to be amortized) vs. upfront discount accounting treatment
- Exception to standard ramp caps for dedicated capacity (this increases capacity reservation exposure)
- Approval for an accelerated commit clause that locks units for 36 months (no churn reallocation).

Prelim estimate: incremental margin hit of ~18–22% on year-1 economics versus standard 3-year prepay. We can consider a stepped discount: 45% on the front-loaded tranche only, with 20% effective off remaining years — lowers the blended hit to ~12–14%.

Recommend: escalate to Vivek for commercial exception plus get Laura to OK from legal/finance on wording. Karthik please prepare the exact P&L delta (spreadsheet) and the recommended contract language for the accelerated commit clause.

Marissa
Head of Sales Ops

Thanks team — quick read. High level: I'm willing to approve an exception if the following conditions are met:

1) Novus signs a 36-month commitment with a 12-month non-refundable front-loaded payment.
2) We add a capacity protection clause that allows Redwood to reallocate unused reserved capacity after a 6-month review window with pro-rated credit, but only after the first 12 months.
3) Novus accepts a performance SLA credit cap (no unlimited failure credits).
4) Finance signs off on revenue recognition path (we'll treat the discount as a contract liability and amortize).

If the customer accepts those, I'll sign off on the 45% discount for the year-1 tranche only — provided legal signs the contract language. Please prepare a concise exec memo (one page) with the blended economics, worst-case revenue exposure, and suggested mitigations. Marissa/Karthik, can you have that ready by EOD Tuesday?

Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference

Team — attached is the one-page memo requested. Summary below:

- Ask: Approve 45% discount on year-1 prepaid tranche representing 55% of total committed spend across a 36-month contract.
- Blended impact: ~13% reduction in blended ASP across term; worst-case FY27 revenue exposure (if usage < committed) is $2.1M cash-on-hand with $0.9M amortized revenue hit.
- Mitigations: 12-month non-refundable front-load, capacity protection with 6-month review window and max 15% reallocation per review, SLA credit caps, pricing true-up clause at mid-term.
- Commercial benefit: Novus is a strategic healthcare anchor customer with potential expansion across 3 additional business units and marketplace co-marketing. Expected ARR uplift yr2–3: +$3.8M.
